articles.title: Patients may miss out on NHS weight-loss jabs in England after GP funding withdrawn
articles.description: Inquiry finds most integrated care boards have scrapped payments to GPs for prescribing and monitoring the drug Patients who are eligible for potentially life-changing weight-loss injections on the NHS risk missing out after most integrated care boards (ICBs) in England withdrew funding for GP services, an investigation has found. The inquiry, conducted by the GP magazine Pulse, found that 21 of 36 ICBs have scrapped payments to practices for prescribing and monitoring Mounjaro, also known as tirzepatide. A further nine never had a local enhanced service and only four still retain one. Continue reading...

articles.author: Kayode Akintola
articles.title: Beating Ebola takes more than medicine – I saw what worked in west Africa a decade ago | Kayode Akintola
articles.description: The outbreak in DR Congo is shaping up to be the worst ever, but the support of local faith leaders – and adequate funding – will be needed to bring it under control Ebola is terrifying: I know, because I lived through the world’s worst outbreak of the disease . That was in west Africa between 2013 and 2016, when anyone infected by the virus had a nearly 40% chance of dying . There were 28,600 cases and 11,300 deaths then. Now a rare strain of Ebola is spreading in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, much more quickly than a decade ago in Sierra Leone, Liberia and neighbouring countries. It is the 17th outbreak in DR Congo and already its worst, with more than 5,000 deaths . The UN is warning that the spread of the disease is outstripping the response, and it is widely expected to become the worst Ebola outbreak in history. There is no proven vaccine or treatment yet for the Bundibugyo variant; almost 50% of those infected have died . Continue reading...

articles.description: Sarah Blaffer Hrdy unpicked Darwinian sexism to rewrite the story of evolution. It was 2014 and Hrdy was conducting an experiment. Having recorded a 63% jump in oxytocin in her saliva after spending hours cuddling the baby, she wanted to find out if something similar would happen to his hormones. It did, although it took a day longer. In her latest book, Father Time: A Natural History of Men and Babies , Hrdy records with justified pride that “this was the first time anyone had demonstrated a bump in oxytocin levels among doting grandparents”.
